subject: Customer QPS leak & Dedicated GPU overrun — exec attention needed
messages:
From: Emily Hale <emily.hale@finicity.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Finicity SRE <ops@finicity.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Apr 2026 09:12:14 -0400
Subject: Re: intermittent 5xx spikes and token queueing (Finicity production)

Rishi —

We started seeing a sustained increase in tail latency and 5xx errors hitting our production endpoints starting ~08:40 ET. Our monitoring shows a sudden jump in QPS for LLM text/generate that looks like a small spike that didn’t attenuate — it ran for about 90 minutes and pushed our requests beyond the reserved quota.

Highlights:
- Reserved QPS (per contract): 1,200
- Observed peak QPS: ~2,600 (sustained for ~90m)
- Error rate: 5xx rose from 0.2% to 4.8% during the spike
- Tail p95 latency doubled from ~180ms to ~420ms

This is impacting our checkout verification flow — we’ve seen a 2.1% increase in failed verifications. We’re in the middle of a merchant reconciliation window and this is high-impact.

Can you confirm whether there was an internal throttling / fallback to shared clusters? We received a 429 body a few times referencing "reserved capacity exceeded". We need immediate remediation and to understand whether this was caused by noisy tenant spillover or an internal retry loop on our side.

I attached a couple of screenshots from our SRE dashboard. We need:
- temporary burst to relieve live traffic
- an incident timeline and root-cause ETA
- a proposal for customer credits/compensation given the outage window

Please escalate as needed — if you want ops/engineering on a call now we’re available.

Thanks,
Emily Hale
Head of SRE, Finicity
Attachment: screenshot-ops-20260407.png (image/png, 420 KB)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Emily Hale <emily.hale@finicity.com>
Cc: Finicity SRE <ops@finicity.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Apr 2026 09:28:05 -0400
Subject: Re: intermittent 5xx spikes and token queueing (Finicity production)

Emily —

Thanks for the heads up and for the screenshots. I’m escalating immediately. Short answers: we see the same signal in platform telemetry and it looks like dedicated pool headroom was exhausted and requests spilled to lower-tier shared hosts (hence the 429s and elevated 5xx rate).

Immediate next steps I’m initiating now:
1) Priyom / SRE will stand up a triage bridge (inviting David Kim) and start a live investigation — confirm whether the source is noisy neighbor or internal retry amplification.
2) Neha will validate whether a temporary burst from the Dedicated overflow budget is available and estimate cost.
3) I’ll coordinate an immediate customer-facing incident note and set up a 30-minute bridge at 10:00 ET if that works for your team.

We’ll also prepare an initial customer credit proposal tied to the outage window; I’ll push for exec approval within the hour.

Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415-555-0147
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 7 Apr 2026 10:02:31 -0400
Subject: Fwd: Re: intermittent 5xx spikes and token queueing (Finicity production)

Forwarding the customer thread and initial telemetry snapshot. Key operational notes (preliminary):
- Dedicated pool utilization hit 99% concurrent tokens at 08:36 ET; autoscaling artifacts caused a delayed provisioning decision and several requests were routed to our shared fallback group.
- We observed two noisy sessions from a third-party integration within Finicity (same account) issuing high-frequency small requests — amplifying the token churn.
- KV cache miss rate climbed significantly which increased per-request compute.

Ask for leadership:
- Authorization to apply a one-time capacity burst (2 extra dedicated nodes for 3 hours) to stabilize customer traffic immediately. We’ll absorb the allocation cost if leadership approves; if not, we’ll propose to bill Finicity for burst usage but recommend absorbing to preserve relationship.
- Approval to offer a 20% credit on invoice for the impacted window pending final RC analysis (adjustable).

I’m attaching the triage notes and a draft mutual-action plan to remediate noisy integration patterns, queueing controls, and a long-term quota uplift path for Finicity.

Attachments: mutual-action-plan-v2.pdf

— Priyom
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 7 Apr 2026 11:14:59 -0400
Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: intermittent 5xx spikes and token queueing (Finicity production)

Team —

I authorize a controlled, one-time burst of 2 dedicated nodes for a 3-hour window to keep Finicity stable while SRE validates root cause. Priyom — proceed and stand up the bridge; confirm start time and post the bridge URL in the thread.

Neha — run a quick cost estimate for the burst and outline the rationale for absorbing versus billing back. I want a recommendation within 60 minutes.

Rishi — prepare the customer-facing note and propose a credit amount; keep the language sympathetic and pragmatic. We should not over-promise beyond the 20% placeholder Priyom mentioned until RC is complete.

David — I’m looping you for visibility to ensure this doesn't cascade into capacity planning with other priority accounts. If we see repeat pattern, we need a short-term quota uplift program.

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Emily Hale <emily.hale@finicity.com>
Cc: Finicity SRE <ops@finicity.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Apr 2026 18:46:00 -0400
Subject: Action plan & immediate relief for today’s incident (Finicity)

Emily —

Thank you for flagging this earlier. Quick summary and next steps (we’ll follow up with a full RCA within 72 hours):

What happened (short): Dedicated pool headroom exhausted during an unexpected QPS amplification (external integration produced high-frequency small requests). Some traffic was routed to shared fallback, producing elevated 429/5xx and increased tail latency.

Actions completed (now):
- Temporary burst applied: +2 dedicated nodes (10:40 ET–13:40 ET) — this stabilized request routing and reduced 5xx to baseline by 11:05 ET.
- Live triage bridge completed; Priyom’s team captured telemetry and identified a noisy session pattern originating from a partner integration.
- We’ve queued a targeted rate-limiting recommendation and a KV cache tuning plan in the attached MAP.

Proposed near-term remediation & customer ask:
- Short-term: Implement partner-side rate limits and apply KV-cache tuning (SRE estimate: 48–72 hours).
- Credits: We propose a one-time 15% credit on April invoice for the 90-minute impact window while RCA completes. If the RCA shows systemic platform issue we will increase credit accordingly.
- Long-term: Discussion to uplift reserved QPS or establish a burst allowance for seasonal windows.

I’ve attached the mutual-action-plan (draft) and we propose a 30-minute executive touchpoint tomorrow at 10:00 ET to review RCA scope and credit mechanics.

Attachments: mutual-action-plan-v2.pdf

Thanks again and apologies for the disruption — we’ll share the formal RCA and corrective timeline within 72 hours.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
